papers.what_it_is: A theory-and-simulation paper that defines dynamic parameterized quantum circuits with probabilistic feedforward, proves a lower bound on the loss variance (absence of barren plateaus) for constant feedforward distance via a statistical-mechanics mapping, and tests ground-state and thermal-state preparation by classical simulation.

existing.note: The quoted statement is the paper's second expressivity observation. It is stated for deterministic feedforward operations that occur only on ancilla qubits on which the loss function has no support. For probabilistic feedforward without ancillas the first observation gives the same conclusion by setting all feedforward probabilities to 0. Both are labelled informal, with a short argument in the text.
existing.value: The authors state that, if one starts from a unitary parameterized quantum circuit and adds ancilla qubits and deterministic feedforward operations on those ancilla qubits, on which the loss function has no support, the resulting dynamic circuit is at least as expressive as the original unitary circuit.
quotes: the resulting parameterized dynamic quantum circuit is at least as expressive as the original unitary parameterized quantum circuit
in which all feedforward operations are deterministic (i.e. happen with probability 1) and only occur on ancilla qubits (qubits on which the loss function has no support)
existing.certainty_reason: The observation is stated with its conditions and a short argument in Section I B 2.

existing.note: The informal Theorem 1 is the stated result. The formal version (Theorem 3.A, and Theorem 12 in Appendix C) adds the conditions that every parameter controls a single operation, that the circuit ensemble is locally scrambling, and that the ensemble has an average entangling power alpha. The lower bound depends on k, f and alpha, and is not constant unless k and f are constant. The informal bound (an alpha over five power of k times f plus one) differs in form from the formal one (a sin squared phi over three factor and an alpha over five power of k times f).
existing.value: The authors state that they prove absence of barren plateaus for local observables under the condition that the feedforward distance f is constant, for circuits with every parameter controlling a single operation, a locally scrambling ensemble, and an average entangling power alpha.
